title: Brainstem & Cerebellum
subtitle: Arousal, coordination and prediction
learningObjectives: Distinguish core brainstem roles in arousal, autonomic control, long tracts and cranial-nerve function.
Explain cerebellar contributions to timing, prediction and error correction beyond movement.
Recognise neurological red flags that should override routine psychological interpretation.

sections.explainSimply: The brainstem keeps vital systems running and helps you stay awake. The cerebellum fine-tunes movement and helps the brain predict what happens next.
sections.explainLikePsychologist: Brainstem nuclei regulate arousal, sleep, autonomic function and cranial nerves. Cerebellar circuits contribute to timing, error correction, learning and aspects of cognition and affect.
sections.advancedClinicalDetail: Ascending neuromodulatory systems influence global cortical state. Cerebello-thalamo-cortical loops support predictive modelling beyond motor control, including language, executive and affective regulation.
sections.thinkOfItLike: The brainstem is the power-and-alertness system; the cerebellum is a precision coach constantly comparing intended and actual performance.
sections.whyPsychologistsCare: Arousal and autonomic state can profoundly shape attention, emotion regulation and test performance.
sections.whenItGoesWrong: Damage may cause altered consciousness, cranial nerve signs, ataxia, dysmetria or cognitive-affective changes.
sections.clinicalPearl: Before interpreting cognition, ask whether the person’s arousal and physiological state permit cognition to work normally.
sections.practicalExample: A person with acute diplopia, dysarthria and gait ataxia should not be conceptualised initially as having anxiety-related dizziness. The combination raises concern for posterior-circulation or brainstem–cerebellar pathology and requires urgent medical assessment.
sections.limitationsCautions: Cerebellar contributions to cognition and affect are real but should not be used to infer a specific cerebellar lesion from nonspecific executive or emotional symptoms. Acute cranial-nerve, consciousness or severe coordination changes require medical evaluation.

quizBank.question: Which structure is especially important for error correction and timing?
quizBank.explanation: The cerebellum compares predicted and actual outcomes to refine timing, coordination and learning.
